title: Descent of an evaluated adjunction without a common level bound
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,Y,\overline X$ and $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr S_W^\tau$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise morphisms [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ and, for $m\ge n\ge1$, derived quotient functors $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Write $t^M_{m,n}:T^W_{m,n}M_m\to M_n$ for the scalar-extension adjunct of the actual transition. 
Assume the actual etale functors $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}\dashv G$ are identified under $e_n$ with the ordinary finite adjunctions, preserving units and counits. Suppose their transitions are
$$t^{FM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m},\qquad t^{GN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},$$
with $q$ the canonical compact-support comparison and $b$ its counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$, let $\mathscr N_W^\tau$ be the full subcategory of systems with every $t_{m,n}$ invertible and every level bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. No common cohomological or Tor interval is required.
Both etale functors preserve $\mathscr N^\mathrm{et}$. On finite-Tor constructible inputs $b$ is the canonical invertible finite exceptional comparison [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]; its identity-index and quotient cocycle agree with the actual system transitions. For $\nu_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to W_{\mathrm{et}}$, with site comparison as in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the actual system adjunction $\nu_W^*\dashv R\nu_{W,*,\bullet}$ restricts to inverse equivalences $\mathscr N_W^{\mathrm{et}}\simeq\mathscr N_W^{\mathrm{proet}}$. The canonical geometric mate
$$\nu_Y^*F\longrightarrow Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}\nu_X^*$$
is invertible on these categories. Transport of $F\dashv G$ therefore defines an adjunction on $\mathscr N^{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose left functor is the displayed proper/open composite, whose finite operations are $Rf_{!,A_n}\dashv Rf^!_{A_n}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and whose unit, counit, triangle identities and quotient-transition formulas are the transported actual system maps. This requires no exceptional right adjoint on all pro-etale derived systems.

source.place: First proof paragraph, normalization, and final paragraph, system adjunction: levelwise finite-Tor restriction, cocycle and etale-origin descent; returned steps 7-10. Agent-formulated ordinary-system refinement; argument allocation and the complete retained argument are in the worker report.

proof.text: Put $C_W=\nu_{W,\bullet}^*$ and $U_W=R\nu_{W,*,\bullet}$. The ordinary semilinear-system calculus supplies $C_W\dashv U_W$ on the unbounded categories, its actual unit $u$, counit $v$, scalar comparisons and evaluations. At level $n$ the comparison inverse image is fully faithful on the entire unbounded derived category: $k$ is algebraically closed, $W$ is finite type, and $A_n$ is finite and killed by a power of the invertible prime $\ell$. For an adjunction with fully faithful left functor, its unit is invertible: the adjunction bijection and the fully faithful Hom bijection identify postcomposition with that unit with a bijection for every test object, and applying this to its source and target gives an inverse. Its counit is invertible on the left functor's essential image by the triangle identities. Thus every $e_nu$ is invertible. If all $K_n$ have etale origin, every $e_nv_K$ is invertible too. Joint conservativity of derived evaluations proves that these actual SYSTEM maps $u$ and $v_K$ are isomorphisms. In particular $C_W$ reflects isomorphisms: evaluate and use full faithfulness at each level.

source.place: Conclusion: unbounded unit and full faithfulness; agent application to actual system maps

proof.text:
The calculus identifies $C_W(t^M_{m,n})$ with $t^{C_WM}_{m,n}$ under $C_{W,n}T^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,n}\cong T^{\mathrm{proet}}_{m,n}C_{W,m}$. Hence $C_W$ preserves normalization. It preserves bounded constructible finite-Tor levels by site comparison. Conversely take $K\in\mathscr N_W^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Each $K_n$ has etale origin by bounded constructible comparison, so Step 1 gives $v_K:C_WU_WK\cong K$. Naturality of the actual reduction map with respect to this system morphism gives, under the same scalar comparison,
$$v_{K,n}\,C_{W,n}(t^{U_WK}_{m,n})=t^K_{m,n}\,T^{\mathrm{proet}}_{m,n}(v_{K,m}).$$
The other three arrows are invertible, so full faithfulness of $C_{W,n}$ implies that $t^{U_WK}_{m,n}$ is invertible. The unbounded finite-Tor reflection theorem applies to $(U_WK)_n$, whose pullback is $K_n$, and gives its bounded constructibility and finite Tor interval. No preliminary lower bound on $(U_WK)_n$ is assumed. We have proved both restrictions and the equivalence $C_W:\mathscr N_W^{\mathrm{et}}\simeq\mathscr N_W^{\mathrm{proet}}$ using the actual $u,v$.

source.place: Conclusion, combined with constructible comparison (Stacks 09AK); explicit normalization square

proof.text: Write $P=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}^{\mathrm{proet}}$. On systems first form the open comparison $C_{\overline X}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}\cong j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}C_X$, then the direct-image mate $C_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*,\bullet}\to Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*,\bullet}C_{\overline X}$. Their composite is an actual transformation $\beta:C_YF\to PC_X$. The semilinear-system calculus constructs these mate words and identifies their evaluations with the ordinary level words. Open comparison is the degreewise comparison with its actual open unit and evaluation counit; it is invertible on unbounded complexes. The other evaluated arrow is the canonical unbounded direct-image mate, invertible because $p$ is finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes. Thus every $e_n\beta$ is invertible, and conservative evaluation makes $\beta$ invertible. This establishes the named geometric comparison, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Canonical counit mate and conclusion; open factor: Stacks 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison

proof.text:
Fix a level $n$, allowing its input intervals to depend on $n$. Open extension preserves bounded constructibility and its finite Tor interval; proper direct image preserves bounded constructibility and changes a Tor interval $[a_n,b_n]$ to $[a_n,b_n+2d]$, where choose $d\ge0$ with $\dim\overline X\le d$ by finite-type dimension finiteness (use $d=0$ for the empty scheme). Apply these results on pro-etale sites. For an etale input in $\mathscr N_X^{\mathrm{et}}$, Step 3 identifies the resulting finite composite with $
u_Y^*F_nM_n$; unbounded reflection gives bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude for $F_nM_n$. For $G_nN_n$, the definition of the finite exceptional functor identifies $
u_X^*G_nN_n$ with $Rf^!_{A_n}(
u_Y^*N_n)$, using the comparison unit. Finite exceptional preservation gives bounded constructibility and a finite Tor interval on this pro-etale value; unbounded reflection again gives them on $G_nN_n$. All schemes and the fixed compactification are in the finite-field setting and separated finite type as required. This proves level preservation for both functors, independently of normalization.

source.place: First sentence: finite exceptional preservation; compact-support preservation and site reflection expanded

proof.text:
On finite-Tor constructible inputs, compact-support coefficient comparison $q$ is invertible and respects successive reductions. Its etale and pro-etale versions correspond: expand it as open scalar comparison followed by the proper counit-defined projection map. Pullback commutes with derived scalar extension in the system calculus; open site comparison preserves the open unit and counit. Mate pasting then identifies the two proper scalar/site words, since both are the mate of the same inverse-image/tensor square. Here the pro-etale finite adjunction $F_n=Rf_{!,n}\dashv G_n=Rf_n^!$ whose units and counits occur in the finite exceptional theorem is, by the definition of $Rf_n^!=
u_X^*f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$, the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction obtained by transporting the ordinary etale adjunction $Rp_*j_!\dashv f^	imes$ along the compact-support site comparison and the full faithfulness of $
u^*$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; the level comparison of Step 3 is that compact-support comparison. The same pasting for $F_n\dashv G_n$, using their assumed counit-compatible evaluated identifications, therefore carries the etale counit mate $b$ to the finite exceptional mate. The finite exceptional theorem states that this mate is invertible and gives its two unit/counit equations and quotient cocycle. Fully faithful level comparison reflects these equalities and isomorphisms. In particular
$$\epsilon_nF_n(b_{m,n})q_{m,n,G_m}=T^Y_{m,n}(\epsilon_m).$$
This equation uniquely characterizes $b$ by the finite adjunction bijection, so it identifies the specified mate, not just an isomorphism between its source and target. Its identity-index and cocycle equations are precisely those of the finite theorem. We use mate pasting for equalities of specified words, not detection of equality of unrelated system maps.

source.place: Last paragraph: coefficient comparisons preserve evaluation, units and counits; explicit mate identification

proof.text: For $M\in\mathscr N_X^{\mathrm{et}}$ the assumed formula $t^{FM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m}$ is a composite of isomorphisms by Step 5. For $N\in\mathscr N_Y^{\mathrm{et}}$ the same argument applies to $t^{GN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m}$. Together with Step 4 this proves both functors preserve the full subcategories. Their transition compatibility is that of their actual system maps from the hypothesis; the identified finite $b$ has the identity-index and quotient cocycle just proved. Restrict the ambient Hom bijections of $F\dashv G$ to these full subcategories. The unit and counit are the same ambient maps and their two triangle equations remain equations in the full subcategories. This restriction requires no common bound.

source.place: Finite normalization and restriction of the assumed actual adjunction

proof.text:
For $M\in\mathscr N_X^{\mathrm{proet}}$, Step 2 gives $C_XU_XM\cong M$. Thus $PM\cong PC_XU_XM\cong C_YFU_XM$, so $P$ preserves the pro-etale subcategories. Put $H=C_XGU_Y$. All factors now preserve their stated domains. On actual system Hom sets use the natural composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(PM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(C_YFU_XM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(FU_XM,U_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(U_XM,GU_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,HN).$$
The first isomorphism uses $\beta$ and $v_{X,M}$; the second and last use the equivalences of Step 2, and the middle is the restricted ambient adjunction. These bijections and their inverses define $P\dashv H$. Define its unit by the image of $1_{PM}$ and counit by the inverse image of $1_{HN}$. Naturality gives the formulas $h\mapsto H(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NP(g)$; applying the inverse equations to identities proves the triangles. Consequently these are transported actual system maps, with triangle identities in the system category itself.

source.place: Transport of the actual adjunction by the constructed equivalences; explicit Hom bijections

proof.text:
Evaluation preserves the units and counits of the site system adjunction and of the assumed etale exceptional adjunction. It also preserves the specified proper/open mate $\beta$. Therefore evaluating the composite Hom construction in Step 7 gives the ordinary finite adjunction with right functor $\nu_X^*G_nR\nu_{Y,*}=Rf^!_{A_n}$ and left functor $Rf_{!,A_n}$. Here evaluation is applied to the constructed unit/counit/mate words; no faithfulness on arbitrary system Hom sets is claimed. The scalar comparisons of $C_W,U_W$ are the specified adjunction mates in the system calculus, so mate pasting carries the assumed transition words to
$$t^{PM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m},\qquad t^{HN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},$$
with finite pro-etale notation on the right. Step 5 identifies their coefficient maps and their identity/cocycle and adjunction equations with the canonical finite ones. Functorial transport preserves the actual triangle equations from Step 6. Every bound used above was attached to one level only; no limit of finite Hom bijections or exceptional right adjoint on all pro-etale systems was introduced.
